simple.meaning: תּוֹעָפָה (tôwʻâphâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “(only in plural collective) weariness , i.e. (by implication) toil ( treasure so obtained) or speed.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Numbers 23:22. The surrounding context includes Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תּוֹעָפָה (H8443) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: תּוֹעָפָה (tôwʻâphâh) / H8443 is traced through Numbers 23:22, Numbers 24:8, Job 22:25, Psalms 95:4 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H8443. toaphah [ תּוֺעָפָה ] noun feminine eminence ; of towering horns (? see Di) לוֺ רְאֵם כְּתוֺעֲפֹת Num 23:22 ; 24:8 , simile of strength of Israel; of peaks לוֺ הָרִים תּוֺעֲפוֺת Psa 95:4 (|| מֶחְקְרֵיאָֿ֑רֶץ ); of silver Job 22:25 לָ֑ךְ תּוֺעָפוֺת כֶּסֶף , very dubious, perhaps heaps or bars (ingots).
